1.title: Compliance and Ethical AI
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Compliance and Ethical A I. This module covers compliance and ethical a i. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. How to map a regulation to architecture choices (G D P R, H I P A A, Fed R A M P). Anthropic's data handling arrangements: retention, Z D R, B A A, residency. Which platform routes meet which regime. Ethical A I: bias, fairness and transparency in design.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lumen Advisory Serves Three Regulated Clients
1.text: Our running case is Lumen Advisory. Lumen Advisory Serves Three Regulated Clients. A European retailer (G D P R), a U S hospital group (H I P A A) and a federal agency (Fed R A M P). Each wants the same assistant; each needs a different platform, contract and data flow.

1.title: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision
1.text: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision. Law is not a certification Claude "has": compliance depends on how and where you process data, the contracts in place and your controls. Always confirm current status with Anthropic and legal counsel.

1.title: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision, continued
1.text: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision, continued. The figure shows this: Three regimes and their architecture responses: G D P R with a data processing addendum, residency and minimization; H I P A A with a B A A and eligible features; Fed R A M P with an authorized platform route.

1.title: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision, continued
1.text: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision, continued. G D P R (E U personal data). Protects: Personal data of people in the E U. Architecture responses: Lawful basis, minimization, D P A with the processor, data residency or transfer mechanism, retention limits, data-subject rights (access, deletion), records of processing. H I P A A (U S health data). Protects: Protected health information (P H I). Architecture responses: B A A with the vendor, H I P A A-ready configuration and eligible features only, access controls and audit logging, minimum necessary data.

1.title: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision, continued
1.text: Compliance Is an Architecture Decision, continued. Fed R A M P (U S federal cloud). Protects: Federal data in cloud services. Architecture responses: Use a Fed R A M P-authorized route, for example Claude through Amazon Bedrock in A W S Gov Cloud or Google Cloud Vertex A I with Assured Workloads; the direct Claude A P I (application programming interface) is not Fed R A M P authorized. Others (P C I D S S, S O C two, sector rules). Protects: Cards, controls, sector data. Architecture responses: Tokenize or avoid card data; evidence from the vendor's attestations.

1.title: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements
1.text: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements. Standard commercial terms. What it means: Customer content from the A P I is not used for training by default; retention is minimal and feature-specific. Notes: Retained data is never used for training without permission. Zero data retention (Z D R). What it means: Anthropic does not store prompts or responses at rest after the response. Notes: Enabled per organization by the account team; individual features are eligible or not; Z D R organizations cannot call the A P I from a browser (use a back end).

1.title: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements, continued
1.text: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements, continued. H I P A A readiness. What it means: Signed B A A plus a H I P A A-enabled organization; encryption, access control and audit logging. Notes: Applies to eligible features only; not every feature qualifies (for example some server tools are not H I P A A eligible). Covered Models. What it means: Designated models require thirty-day retention. Notes: Z D R is not available for them unless Anthropic authorizes it. Data residency. What it means: Choose inference geography (inference geo, for example global or U S). Notes: Track by usage reports. Cloud platforms. What it means: On Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud (Google managed) the cloud provider is the data processor; their B A A, D P A, residency and certifications apply. Notes: Feature availability differs by platform.

1.title: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements, continued
1.text: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements, continued. The figure shows this: Mapping a requirement to a route: Z D R on eligible features, B A A with H I P A A readiness, Fed R A M P through Gov Cloud or Vertex with Assured Workloads, regional processing through residency settings. Design practices for any regime. Classify data; send the minimum to the model; mask or tokenize P I I before the prompt and restore it after (also possible inside a sandbox). Keep logs free of regulated content or protect and expire them.

1.title: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements, continued
1.text: Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements, continued. Enforce access control per user (Module eight); encrypt in transit and at rest. Document data flows, subprocessors, retention and deletion paths. Plan incident response and audit evidence. Check feature eligibility (Z D R or H I P A A) before using a feature in a regulated workflow. Exam tip: Match the regime to the route and contract: H I P A A equals B A A plus H I P A A-ready eligible features; Fed R A M P equals a Fed R A M P-authorized cloud route, not the direct A P I; G D P R equals D P A, minimization and residency. "Any A P I call is compliant" is the distractor.

1.title: Ethical AI: Bias, Fairness and Transparency
1.text: Ethical A I: Bias, Fairness and Transparency. The figure shows this: Ethical A I in design: bias testing, fairness across groups, transparency through disclosure and citations, and accountability through human oversight.

1.title: Ethical AI: Bias, Fairness and Transparency, continued
1.text: Ethical A I: Bias, Fairness and Transparency, continued. Bias. Test outputs across demographic and language groups; include diverse cases in evals; review prompts and data for skew; measure disparity (error rate gaps). Fairness. Define the fairness criterion with stakeholders (equal error rates, equal opportunity); keep humans decisive for consequential decisions; provide appeal paths. Transparency. Disclose A I involvement; show citations and sources; explain limits and confidence; document the system (what it does and does not do). Accountability. Name an owner; keep audit trails; qualified human review for high-risk uses. Privacy. Minimization, consent, retention limits. Safety and non-harm. Guardrails, red-teaming, incident response.

2.title: Ethical AI: Bias, Fairness and Transparency, continued
2.text: Ethical A I: Bias, Fairness and Transparency, continued. Provenance. Claude outputs can carry watermarks and content credentials: a mark is a signal, not proof; absence proves nothing. Fairness is measured, not assumed: add subgroup metrics to the eval suite. High-risk decisions about people need a qualified human who can change the result, and disclosure to the affected person. Be honest about limitations to users and stakeholders (Module fifteen). Exam tip: Match the regime to the route and contract: B A A and eligible features, Fed R A M P-authorized route, D P A with residency. Exam tip: Fairness is measured: add subgroup metrics to the eval suite and keep a human decisive for consequential decisions.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. G D P R: Lawful basis, minimization, D P A, residency, retention, rights. H I P A A: B A A, H I P A A-ready org, eligible features only, audit logging. Fed R A M P: Authorized route: Bedrock in Gov Cloud or Vertex with Assured Workloads; direct A P I not authorized. Z D R: No storage at rest; per org; feature eligibility; no browser calls. Covered Models: thirty-day retention; no Z D R. Cloud platforms: Provider is the processor; its contracts apply. Practice: Classify, minimize, mask, access control, document, incident plan. Ethics: Subgroup testing, human decisions, disclosure, citations, accountability. Marks: Signal not proof.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A U S hospital group wants an assistant that processes patient notes through the Claude A P I. What is required? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. H I P A A needs a B A A and eligible features; other options do not satisfy it.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A federal agency needs Fed R A M P High for a Claude-based service. Which route fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. The direct A P I is not Fed R A M P authorized; use an authorized cloud route.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. A European retailer must limit personal data in prompts and prove processing terms. Which two actions help? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and D. Minimization and a D P A with residency address G D P R obligations.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A team enables a server tool in a H I P A A workflow without checking eligibility. What is the risk? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Check feature eligibility before using it in regulated flows.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. What does a zero data retention arrangement mean for browser-based calls? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Cross-origin browser requests are rejected for Z D R organizations.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A hiring-support assistant shows a higher error rate for resumes in one language. What should the architect do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Fairness requires measuring disparities and acting on them.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Which statement about A I-generated-content marks (watermarks, content credentials) is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. A detected mark is a useful signal rather than proof, and a missing mark proves nothing about who wrote the content.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. Models designated as Covered Models require what retention? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Covered Models require thirty-day retention, so zero data retention is not available for them unless Anthropic authorizes it.

2.title: Practice Question 9
2.text: Question nine. A consultant says "Claude is H I P A A compliant" and proposes using any A P I feature. Which response is right? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Regimes are met by contract, configuration and controls.

2.title: Practice Question 10
2.text: Question ten. Which practice best supports transparency to end users? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Transparency means disclosing A I involvement, showing citations and sources, and being honest about the system's limits.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all ten answers. Question one: A. Question two: C. Question three: A and D. Question four: B. Question five: A. Question six: B. Question seven: D. Question eight: C. Question nine: D. Question ten: D. In the next module, we continue the course.
